newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: JG-Telecom plans NZ$1 bln shr repurchase.
newsitem.headline: JG-Telecom plans NZ$1 bln shr repurchase.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Thursday it planned a NZ$1 billion share repurchase programme over a one year period starting in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997.

Chairman Peter Shirtcliffe said the company's balance sheet was well able to withstand such a programme and it was intended to reduce the company's average cost of capital. "Our intentions reflect the strength of Telecom's financial position and our confidence in the business outlook," he said.
"We plan to proceed expeditiously while, at the same time, ensuring there is no distortion to the market price of Telecom shares," he said.
Repurchases will be subject to detailed procedures and disclosure requirements under the Companies Act, he said.

The repurchase programme will encompass the quarter holdings each of Bell Atlantic and Ameritech so that their combined holdings do not exceed 49.9 percent and breach the terms of Telecom's Kiwi Share arrangement with the government at the time of its 1990 privatisation.
Shirtcliffe said that Telecom intended to retain a strong balance sheet and continue with the current dividend policy as the repurchase programme proceeded.

The first repurchases were intended to commence in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997, beginning at an appropriate time after the announcement of the third quarter result in February. Telecom has a March 31 balance date.
Telecom has 1.89 billion shares on issue.
Telecom has a target to keep the ratio of net debt to net debt plus equity within a 40-45 percent range.

Telecom last had a capital reduction in March 1994 when it cancelled one in five shares. Analysts considered Telecom had largely exhausted revenue reserves at that point so that any future capital reduction would be treated as a realisation of gains for tax purposes.
